A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LASER and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F. The retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and forecasting experiments on Navier-Stokes, Shallow-Water, and SST, together with ablations and sensor-initialization sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on iterative co-training, policy-induced observation distributions, and heuristic sensing strategies.

M1.justification: Section 5.4 adds an evaluated co-training variant that alternates world-model fine-tuning on policy-collected observations with policy reoptimization. The base architecture, GRPO procedure, filtering, and predictive rewards remain unchanged; the Gaussian-decoder wording clarifies the existing model.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Navier-Stokes viscosity regimes, Shallow-Water, and SST for sparse reconstruction and forecasting. The additional studies vary training, sensor-selection procedures, and rollout initialization within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds entropy-based, error-based, and dynamics-based sensing comparators in Table 11 and Appendix F.4. Their shared reconstruction model provides a substantial new comparison of sensing strategies. The original AROMA, DiffusionPDE, PhySense, and PPO comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include NS rollouts initialized at t = 1 from policy-selected observations with 256 sensors, and heuristic comparisons holding the world model fixed. Existing splits, training budgets, and benchmark protocols are retained. Distinguishing MSErollout from MSErecon clarifies existing metrics rather than replacing them.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 substantially expands the analyses with co-training tests, a targeted examination of policy-induced distribution shift, and controlled heuristic comparisons probing the value of proactive sensing. Appendix F.4 adds corresponding qualitative evidence. The earlier ablations and initialization-sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix F.1 retains the same means and standard deviations over three random sensor initializations, with Table 11 renumbered to Table 14. No additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests accompany the new experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 9–11 and Figure 12 add substantial findings on co-training, distribution shift, and heuristic performance. For example, SST co-training errors are 0.6727/0.6934 for 100/50 sensors, versus retained LASER values of 0.6932/0.7184. Earlier table entries remain unchanged; Table 8's 10^-3 scale becomes explicit. The new t = 1 rollout results are separate from the original benchmark.

T1.justification: Appendix F.4 adds mathematical definitions of score-proportional heuristic sampling and the error/dynamics score functions. The original POMDP, world-model objective, diffusion formulation, and GRPO mathematics are retained, with no new proofs or guarantees. The standard MSE formulas are explanatory additions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about POMDP-based active sensing, predictive latent modeling, and reconstruction superiority. The new analyses support these claims without redefining the stated core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets co-training as mitigating world-model constraints, policy-induced observations as improving latent predictions, and heuristic failures as evidence for proactive planning. These substantive explanations are new. The conclusion's limitations concerning model fidelity and computational overhead remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 newly discloses GRPO group size 8 and batch size 512, comprising 64 groups. Appendix F.4 documents heuristic scoring and sampling. The main text clarifies decoder likelihood and evaluation details. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously used settings.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography remove Poli et al. (2022), Transform once: Efficient operator learning in frequency domain. Other reference edits concern bibliographic metadata, while the positioning relative to reconstruction and sensor-placement research remains stable.

P1.justification: Targeted edits clarify the Gaussian likelihood, reconstruction loss, and distinction between forecasting and online reconstruction. Section 5.4 expands, a heuristic-comparison appendix subsection is inserted, and the publication footer changes. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the world-model data-flow diagram, Figure 3; heuristic visualizations, Figure 12; and Tables 9–11. Existing displays are retained with relocation and renumbering, clearer metric captions, and added time arrows in the final reconstruction figures. The visual format remains largely consistent.

improvement.justification: The new controlled comparisons and adaptation analyses strengthen empirical support for LASER, while clearer metrics, the data-flow diagram, and disclosed GRPO settings improve readability and reproducibility. The gain is limited: co-training schedules and Table 11's temporal aggregation remain underspecified, and the broad interpretation of harmless distribution shift rests on one tested NS configuration.
